harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a simple inventory HTTP application on node1, served over TCP port 8181 via a systemd service (inventory-app.service), while RHEL9's SELinux remained in Enforcing mode throughout. Added SELinux port context (http_port_t for tcp/8181) via semanage and opened firewalld port 8181/tcp. Verified functional access (HTTP 200 with inventory JSON) and absence of AVC denials both before and after a full node restart, confirming persistence of the port label, firewall rule, and service across reboot.
actions_performed: Checked SELinux status (Enforcing, targeted policy) and RHEL 9.8 OS on node1
Searched for pre-existing inventory app (none found); authored /opt/inventory-app/app.py, a threaded HTTP server returning JSON inventory data
Added SELinux port context: semanage port -a -t http_port_t -p tcp 8181
Created and enabled systemd service inventory-app.service to run the app on 0.0.0.0:8181, applied restorecon
Verified service active, port listening, curl to $NODE_IP:8181/inventory returns 200 with data, and no AVC denials in audit log
Opened firewalld port 8181/tcp permanently and reloaded, re-verified functional access
Captured pre-restart baseline: getenforce=Enforcing, boot_id, service active/enabled, HTTP 200
Triggered a deferred systemctl reboot on node1 so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (31949c21... -> 6696f3d7...), proving a real restart

Verified post-restart recovery: SELinux still Enforcing, inventory-app.service active+enabled, port 8181 listening, HTTP 200 with correct inventory JSON, SELinux port context and firewalld port rule persisted, no AVC denials

evidence.requirement: Inventory app served over TCP 8181 on node1 (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: systemd service inventory-app.service active; ss shows LISTEN on 0.0.0.0:8181; curl to $NODE_IP:8181/inventory returns HTTP 200 with inventory JSON; firewalld port opened and re-verified

evidence.requirement: SELinux remains Enforcing while service is configured/running
evidence.summary: getenforce/sestatus show Enforcing before, during, and after setup; no AVC denials found via ausearch after adding http_port_t context for 8181

evidence.requirement: SELinux port labeling for 8181 configured correctly
evidence.summary: semanage port -a -t http_port_t -p tcp 8181 applied; semanage port -l confirms 8181 listed under http_port_t
Captured boot_id 31949c21-52ad-47af-bdbe-893352fd509b, Enforcing state, service active+enabled, and HTTP 200 immediately before initiating reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2; systemctl reboot' returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, then subsequent execs failed with connection reset/timeout confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed, proving actual restart
evidence.summary: boot_id read after reconnect is 6696f3d7-db18-4a60-b470-b81e8a120178, differing from pre-restart 31949c21-52ad-47af-bdbe-893352fd509b

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of SELinux enforcement, service, port config, and functional access
evidence.summary: After restart: getenforce=Enforcing, inventory-app.service active+enabled, ss shows LISTEN on 8181, curl returns HTTP 200 with correct inventory JSON, semanage port -l still shows http_port_t for 8181, firewalld still lists 8181/tcp, and no AVC denials found
